task.name: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the model quarantines that model for the rest of the run
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2950
---
## What
Slice 3 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. When a dispatch is refused for a reason that is a property of the configuration rather than the request — the account may not call this model — that model is quarantined for the remainder of the run: no later dispatch in that run reaches it, and the run continues on the remaining models. The initial availability classification (#2949) and the pre-dispatch empty-pool stop (#2950) are the earlier slices; this one covers what the router learns *from* a refusal it did not predict.

Quarantine is enforced at the one dispatch seam every agent call already passes through (`run_agent`, which is also where the configured-vs-resolved identity is stamped once per dispatch), not at each call site. Phases, roles and flows are covered because they dispatch through the seam, not because each was edited.

## Why
Availability resolution cannot be perfect: a provider may publish no catalog (unverified), the catalog may lag the provider's actual policy, or the answer may go stale mid-sprint. An explicit refusal is stronger evidence than any prior state. Without quarantine, a sprint meets the identical refusal once per story, paying WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan each time — which is exactly what happened across four stories on 2026-09-04. The existing transient-failure quarantine in `provider_health` is adjacent (reviewer-only, time-windowed, pattern-matched on capacity and rate-limit strings) and does not cover configuration refusals. See #2914.

The first attempt at this story (sprint `1b75c9e1294c`, 2026-09-08) escalated in plan review after five plans, each rejected for one more dispatch surface the previous plan had not enumerated. The earlier criteria asked for completeness over every call site, which no plan can demonstrate. This revision names one enforcement seam and treats a dispatch that bypasses it as a bug in that dispatch, outside this story.

## Acceptance criteria
- A dispatch refused because the account may not call the selected model is classified as a configuration refusal, distinct from a request-level or transient failure. The classification does not depend on matching one provider's message text: a refusal the classifier cannot attribute is treated as transient and retried within the existing bounded retry budget, never quarantined and never retried unboundedly.
- Quarantine is recorded and enforced at the shared dispatch seam. A quarantined identity requested through the seam is refused before any provider call is made, and the refusal is a routing outcome (see below). The identity checked is the identity actually dispatched: when a runner substitutes a fallback model or transport internally, the substituted identity is checked the same way, and a fallback onto a quarantined identity is refused the same way.
- Callers that are not a dev, review or validate phase are covered through the seam with no site-specific code. The decomposition assessment, the escalation advisor and the landing conflict resolver are pinned as non-regression cases: a test shows a quarantined identity is refused for at least one of the first two and for the conflict resolver. A dispatch that reaches a provider without passing the seam is a bug in that dispatch and is out of scope here.
- Quarantine is scoped to the run and survives a re-exec of the same run: it is keyed by an identifier that is stable across process generations, so a story inherited across that boundary still sees it. The next run resolves availability afresh (#2949) rather than inheriting a quarantine that may no longer hold.
- A refusal of a quarantined identity is a routing outcome, not an agent failure. It carries a distinct marker so that transient-failure and retry classifiers in any phase never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.
- Every exclusion a quarantine causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it. Quarantine applies to an unverified model as much as to one the availability answer called available: the refusal converts unverified to unavailable for the rest of that run.
- The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend, naming the excluded models, where none do — the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
- The existing reviewer-only transient quarantine in `provider_health` keeps its current behaviour.

## Example
```
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  ✗ DEV   refused — account may not call openai/gpt-5.4/cli under codex
          ChatGPT-account auth (HTTP 400). Quarantined for the rest of run 68aec168166d.
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.6-terra  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.51  5m 02s
  ... later story, same run, non-phase caller ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded for escalation advisor — quarantined after configuration refusal on issue-2775
```

resolutions.answer: Key the quarantine by the sprint's stable identity: the sprint_id that names .forge/sprints/<id>/ and survives re-exec process generations. Do NOT use sprint_run_id (regenerated per generation) or the per-story state.run_id. Thread it explicitly through the coordinator API (your option 2), no thread-local context. A standalone single-story invocation outside any sprint has no sprint_id; scope quarantine to its own run_id so it still applies within that invocation. A new sprint has a new sprint_id, so nothing is inherited.
resolutions.assumption: I will implement the quarantine store keyed on a logical-run-id that is: (1) generated once at sprint entry and shared across all stories in that sprint, (2) stable across os.execv re-execution boundaries via persistence, and (3) threaded through every coordinator entry point (run_task, run_from_dev, run_from_review, run_review_only) as an explicit parameter rather than relying on thread-local context variables. For standalone runs (outside sprint), I will use a per-run identifier scoped to that single coordinator invocation.
resolutions.criterion: Quarantine is scoped to the run and survives a re-exec of the same run: it is keyed by an identifier that is stable across process generations
options_considered: Use state.run_id as-is: simpler locally but breaks the multi-story same-run requirement — stories cannot see each other's quarantine entries.
Compute a logical-run-id from sprint metadata and thread it explicitly through the coordinator API: adds parameter threading but ensures clarity and testability.
Use thread-local context vars for in-sprint dispatches and explicit params for out-of-sprint: hybrid approach, but harder to test and reason about.
resolutions.undefined_case: The plan uses state.run_id as the quarantine key, but state.run_id is independently generated for each story in a sprint by coordinator.engine.run_task, not shared across stories. The sprint runner receives sprint_run_id but does not thread it to run_task. After re-exec via os.execv, later stories in the same sprint would have no way to consult the quarantine records written by earlier stories under their own run_ids. This defeats the 'same run' isolation that AC requires.

correspondences.description: When an API profile has a quarantined fallback model in its preference list, the primary model can fail fallback-eligible and run_api_agent still dispatches the quarantined fallback model.

When a DEV dispatch itself discovers a configuration refusal, the model is quarantined but the same failed result is returned to DEV, so the story can end on that routing refusal instead of continuing on another available model in the run.

The regression case named for the escalation advisor and decomposition assessment directly calls runner_cli.run_agent, so those caller paths can stop dispatching through the seam without this test failing.

When a configuration refusal is first discovered by a dispatch inside the DEV phase, the identity is quarantined and the retry is refused at the seam, but the story itself ends on that routing refusal rather than continuing on the remaining eligible models, because no routing checkpoint exists after the post-plan reseat.

The active-story label used to attribute quarantine records is a single module-global slot written by every concurrent run_task, so with sprint stories running in parallel on the ThreadPoolExecutor (sprint/runner.py:7573, max_workers=max_parallel) a refusal in one story is persisted to .forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml and rendered in every routing exclusion with another concurrently-running story's slug.

The quarantine checks and learn calls inside _maybe_run_api_fallback, and the _learn_from_refusal call on the API-transport branch of run_agent, do not pass the caller's quiet flag, so routing exclusion and quarantine lines are logged even when the dispatch was invoked quiet.

After a process re-exec, sprint resume dispatches through run_from_dev or run_from_review without activating the persisted sprint quarantine, so a model quarantined earlier in the same sprint can reach the provider again.
A native API preference list invokes a quarantined fallback model and loses a configuration refusal from the primary whenever a later fallback succeeds.

Structured entitlement refusals from single-shot API adapters and HTTP 400 tool-loop calls reach the dispatch seam without refusal evidence or escape as exceptions, so the refused model is not quarantined.

An unattributable structured refusal is classified as transient but retains its original failure code and text, causing the DEV transient classifier to reject it as non-retryable instead of spending the bounded retry allowance.

When DEV first discovers a configuration refusal, the identity is recorded as quarantined but the current story enters infrastructure-abort handling instead of re-seating onto another eligible DEV model.
A quarantined reviewer refused at the seam is classified as a crash, included in failed reviewer metadata, and persisted as an unsuccessful capability attempt.

When a story has already cached its routing decision, a later quarantine exclusion at the dispatch seam is only logged and returned as an AgentResult, leaving that story's routing decision showing the model as included.

handoff.summary: Implemented configuration-refusal quarantine in three layers. A new stdlib-only `refusal_types.py` classifies a refused dispatch as configuration or transient from the provider's HTTP status plus its own machine token (`type`/`code`), never its message text; anything it cannot attribute stays transient and keeps its bounded retry budget, and 401 is excluded because a rejected credential belongs to the auth circuit breaker. `model_quarantine.py` was rewritten into a run-scoped store keyed by the sprint id that names `.forge/sprints/<id>/` (per the resolved gap — threaded via the coordinator's existing `sprint_name` parameter, no thread-local), persisted to `.forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml` so a re-exec inherits it and a new sprint starts clean. The central design move is `model_availability.apply_quarantine`, which folds a quarantine into the availability answer at `resolve_story_availability` / `resolve_agent_availability`: routing pools, the launch gate, the post-plan checkpoint and the `routing_decision` block therefore enforce and report it with no code of their own, and `unverified` is converted to `unavailable` for free. Enforcement and learning both sit at the one dispatch seam (`runners.cli.run_agent`), which covers the escalation advisor, decomposition assessment and landing conflict resolver without site-specific code, plus explicit checks on fallback models/transports the runner substitutes internally. A refused quarantined dispatch is a routing outcome: measured `$0.00`, `failure_code=model_quarantined`, the `MODEL_QUARANTINED:` no-output marker registered with `coordinator.agent_failure`, and a new `routing` failure category — so no retry classifier re-dispatches it, nothing reaches the model's capability history, and the story is not charged a dev or review failure. The codex runner now carries structured `refusal_evidence` instead of matching prose, the API runner reads the same off SDK exceptions, and `provider_health` is untouched.

commits.message: feat(quarantine): quarantine a model the account may not call, for the rest of the run (#2951)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the selected model is classified as a configuration refusal, distinct from a request-level or transient failure. The classification does not depend on matching one provider's message text; an unattributable refusal is treated as transient and retried within the existing bounded retry budget, never quarantined and never retried unboundedly.
acceptance_criteria.notes: `refusal_types.classify_refusal` reads only `http_status` and the normalised `type`/`code` tokens; `detail` (the provider's prose) is carried for the operator and never consulted. Requires both a recognised denial token and a consistent status, so a denial token on a 429 is transient. Default for missing/unknown evidence is transient, which routes into the unchanged retry path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Quarantine is recorded and enforced at the shared dispatch seam. A quarantined identity requested through the seam is refused before any provider call, and the refusal is a routing outcome. The identity checked is the identity actually dispatched, including a runner-substituted fallback model or transport.
acceptance_criteria.notes: `_quarantine_refusal` runs at the top of `run_agent` before any transport branch, and again inside `_maybe_run_api_fallback` for the legacy `api_fallback` profile and each `fallback_models` entry. `_learn_from_refusal` records at each of the five dispatch points, keyed on the profile actually dispatched (so a fallback's refusal quarantines the fallback, not the primary). Tests assert the provider runner is never called.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Callers that are not a dev, review or validate phase are covered through the seam with no site-specific code. The decomposition assessment, the escalation advisor and the landing conflict resolver are pinned as non-regression cases.
acceptance_criteria.notes: No caller-side code was added anywhere. `TestNonPhaseCallers` drives the landing conflict resolver end-to-end through `workspace._resolve_merge_conflicts` (asserting it aborts the merge with no claude/codex/api call), and covers the escalation advisor and decomposition assessment profiles at the seam.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Quarantine is scoped to the run and survives a re-exec of the same run, keyed by an identifier stable across process generations. The next run resolves availability afresh.
acceptance_criteria.notes: `quarantine_run_key` returns `sprint:<sprint_name>` when in a sprint (the id that names `.forge/sprints/<id>/`, already threaded into `run_task`) and `run:<run_id>` standalone — exactly the operator's answer in the resolved gap. Records persist to `.forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml`; `activate()` on the same key reloads from disk, a different key starts clean. Tested for re-exec, later-story inheritance, and new-sprint isolation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A refusal of a quarantined identity is a routing outcome, not an agent failure. It carries a distinct marker so retry/transient classifiers never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Distinct marker is `failure_code=model_quarantined` plus the `MODEL_QUARANTINED:` output marker, registered in `agent_failure._NO_OUTPUT_MARKERS`. That makes `produced_model_output()` False, which is the existing mechanism routing it to NO_JUDGMENT / infrastructure-abort taint and out of every router-consumed aggregate. New `CATEGORY_ROUTING` is checked before `startup_failure` so it is never reported as a launcher failure. Cost is a measured $0.00, not cost-unknown. `provider_health.classify_provider_shape_failure` returns None for it (asserted).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every exclusion a quarantine causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it. Quarantine applies to an unverified model as much as to an available one.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The overlay writes a `ModelAvailability(state=unavailable, reason="quarantined after configuration refusal on <story>: <reason>")`, which flows into `RoutingEvidence.availability_exclusions` via the unchanged #2950 path, so the reason lands in the routing decision and the operator-facing exclusion lines. Applies to available, unverified, and identities with no prior answer at all (added, not skipped).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend naming the excluded models where none do — the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Met for every routing boundary that exists: because a quarantine reads as an availability answer, the per-story resolution, the pinned-role check, the preflight reseat, and the post-plan checkpoint's `incumbent_unavailable` reroute all continue on what is left, and an emptied phase takes #2950's existing routing stop verbatim ($0.00, SKIPPED, excluded models named). `TestCoordinatorSeam` asserts this end-to-end through `run_task`. The gap: a refusal discovered *inside* the DEV phase has no re-seat checkpoint after it in this codebase — the identity is quarantined and the retry is refused cheaply at the seam, but the story ends on the routing refusal rather than re-seating mid-DEV. Adding a mid-DEV reroute is a distinct mechanism (a DEV-phase analogue of the post-plan checkpoint) and is outside this story's named seam; every later story in the run does route around the model.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The existing reviewer-only transient quarantine in provider_health keeps its current behaviour.
acceptance_criteria.notes: provider_health.py is unmodified; TestAdjacentMechanismsUnchanged pins both its capacity classification and that a quarantine refusal is not a provider-health signal.

story_deviations: Replaced the prior commit's thread-local quarantine context and `logical_run_id` parameter on `run_task`. The gap answer forbids thread-local context, and the coordinator already threads `sprint_name` — the sprint's stable identity — so no new parameter was needed.

Replaced the prior commit's provider-message-text classifier (`runner_codex._is_configuration_refusal`, `model_quarantine.classify_configuration_refusal`) with structured evidence, because the first AC forbids classifying on one provider's message text. The prior commit also called `profile_dispatch_key(profile)` with one argument against a two-argument signature, which would have raised on every dispatch.

Added `CATEGORY_ROUTING` to `agent_failure.ALLOWED_FAILURE_CATEGORIES`. The AC calls the refusal a routing outcome rather than an agent failure, and none of the six existing categories says that; without it the refusal would have recorded as `process`.
deferred_items: Mid-DEV re-seat after a configuration refusal discovered in the DEV phase itself — see the PARTIAL criterion above. Worth a follow-up issue if the operator wants the example's within-story model swap at DEV rather than at the post-plan checkpoint.

Only the codex CLI runner and the API runner populate `AgentResult.refusal_evidence`. The claude and gemini CLI runners have no pre-generation structured-refusal parser today, so a configuration refusal on those transports classifies as transient (the safe direction) until one is added.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 addressed the single P1: a blocking [test_mirrors_source] convention violation on `src/theforge/refusal_types.py`, which had no `tests/test_refusal_types.py`. Its coverage existed but sat inside `tests/test_model_quarantine.py` as a `TestClassifier` class, because the feature started there. Created the mirror file, moved the classifier coverage into it, and deepened it around the two properties the module exists to hold: provider prose is never evidence (four message-text cases including the trap where the denial token appears as prose), and anything unattributable stays transient (no evidence, bare status with no token, unrecognised token, denial token on 429/5xx, 401, and `invalid_request_error` alone). Added the payload-reader cases the dispatch seam depends on — every status spelling providers use, a deeper payload not erasing a shallower one's status, a non-status number not read as a status, non-mapping entries skipped rather than raising, and a bounded detail. `test_model_quarantine.py` retains the store, seam, non-phase callers and coordinator boundary, with its docstring updated to point at the mirror and explain the split. No source behaviour changed in this iteration; the iteration-1 implementation is unmodified.

Records persist to `.forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml`; same key reloads from disk, different key starts clean. Tested for re-exec, later-story inheritance, and new-sprint isolation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A refusal of a quarantined identity is a routing outcome, not an agent failure. It carries a distinct marker so retry/transient classifiers never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Distinct marker is `failure_code=model_quarantined` plus the `MODEL_QUARANTINED:` output marker registered in `agent_failure._NO_OUTPUT_MARKERS`, which makes `produced_model_output()` False — the existing mechanism routing it to NO_JUDGMENT / infrastructure-abort taint and out of every router-consumed aggregate. New `CATEGORY_ROUTING` is checked before `startup_failure`. Cost is a measured $0.00. `provider_health.classify_provider_shape_failure` returns None for it (asserted).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every exclusion a quarantine causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it. Quarantine applies to an unverified model as much as to an available one.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The overlay writes `ModelAvailability(state=unavailable, reason="quarantined after configuration refusal on <story>: <reason>")`, flowing into `RoutingEvidence.availability_exclusions` via the unchanged #2950 path. Applies to available, unverified, and identities with no prior answer at all.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend naming the excluded models where none do — the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Met for every routing boundary that exists: because a quarantine reads as an availability answer, the per-story resolution, the pinned-role check, the preflight reseat and the post-plan checkpoint's `incumbent_unavailable` reroute all continue on what is left, and an emptied phase takes #2950's routing stop verbatim ($0.00, SKIPPED, excluded models named). `TestCoordinatorSeam` asserts this end-to-end through `run_task`. The gap is unchanged from iteration 1: a refusal discovered inside the DEV phase has no re-seat checkpoint after it, so the identity is quarantined and the retry refused cheaply at the seam, but the story ends on the routing refusal rather than re-seating mid-DEV. Every later story in the run does route around the model.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The existing reviewer-only transient quarantine in provider_health keeps its current behaviour.
acceptance_criteria.notes: provider_health.py is unmodified; TestAdjacentMechanismsUnchanged pins both its capacity classification and that a quarantine refusal is not a provider-health signal.

story_deviations: Replaced the prior commit's thread-local quarantine context and `logical_run_id` parameter on `run_task`. The gap answer forbids thread-local context, and the coordinator already threads `sprint_name` — the sprint's stable identity — so no new parameter was needed.

Replaced the prior commit's provider-message-text classifier (`runner_codex._is_configuration_refusal`, `model_quarantine.classify_configuration_refusal`) with structured evidence, because the first AC forbids classifying on one provider's message text. The prior commit also called `profile_dispatch_key(profile)` with one argument against a two-argument signature, which would have raised on every dispatch.

Added `CATEGORY_ROUTING` to `agent_failure.ALLOWED_FAILURE_CATEGORIES`. The AC calls the refusal a routing outcome rather than an agent failure, and none of the six existing categories says that; without it the refusal would have recorded as `process`.
deferred_items: Mid-DEV re-seat after a configuration refusal discovered in the DEV phase itself — see the PARTIAL criterion above. Worth a follow-up issue if the operator wants the example's within-story model swap at DEV rather than at the post-plan checkpoint.

Only the codex CLI runner and the API runner populate `AgentResult.refusal_evidence`. The claude and gemini CLI runners have no pre-generation structured-refusal parser today, so a configuration refusal on those transports classifies as transient (the safe direction) until one is added.

`make dev-check` reports 17 failures, all pre-existing sandbox-environment failures in test_sprint_lock.py, test_sprint_reexec_collision.py and test_cut_rc_isolation.py (multiprocessing semaphore and mktemp `Operation not permitted`). None touch this change; the failure mode is `PermissionError` from `multiprocessing/synchronize.py`, not an assertion. Pass count rose from 11366 to 11413 with the new mirror.

knowledge_debrief.did: Made the quarantine record and its rendered exclusion reason carry the originating story slug rather than only the synthetic dispatch-identity key, so the routing line resolves back to the story an operator can go read.

Checked that a quarantine only ever produces an exclusion whose remedy is derivable — it names the identity, the status, the provider token and the story — rather than advertising a stop an operator cannot act on.

Chose to fold quarantine into the availability answer instead of adding a second exclusion rule, specifically so the startup gate, per-story routing and the post-plan checkpoint state one message for one condition rather than three near-misses of it.
No optional callback signatures or trial-call arity probing are involved anywhere in this change.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The quarantine core is close, but API fallback/evidence paths and the mid-DEV continuation requirement still miss acceptance criteria. | [anthropic-fable-cli] Solid seam-enforced quarantine with strong classifier and store coverage, but AC 7 is only partially satisfied (a refusal discovered inside the DEV phase ends the story instead of continuing it on remaining models — the spec's own example scenario), and the new module-global active-story label races under parallel sprint execution, mis-attributing persisted quarantine records. Gate verdict PASS at reviewed HEAD was relied on; no full gate rerun. | [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The quarantine works on tested fresh-run paths, but multiple runtime entry points, fallback paths, retry paths, and accounting paths violate the run-scoped routing contract.

findings.description: When an API profile has a quarantined fallback model in its preference list, the primary model can fail fallback-eligible and run_api_agent still dispatches the quarantined fallback model.

When a single-shot API provider returns a structured entitlement refusal such as HTTP 400 with model_not_found, the result reaches the dispatch seam with refusal_evidence=None and no quarantine is recorded.

When a DEV dispatch itself discovers a configuration refusal, the model is quarantined but the same failed result is returned to DEV, so the story can end on that routing refusal instead of continuing on another available model in the run.

The regression case named for the escalation advisor and decomposition assessment directly calls runner_cli.run_agent, so those caller paths can stop dispatching through the seam without this test failing.

When a configuration refusal is first discovered by a dispatch inside the DEV phase, the identity is quarantined and the retry is refused at the seam, but the story itself ends on that routing refusal rather than continuing on the remaining eligible models, because no routing checkpoint exists after the post-plan reseat.

The active-story label used to attribute quarantine records is a single module-global slot written by every concurrent run_task, so with sprint stories running in parallel on the ThreadPoolExecutor (sprint/runner.py:7573, max_workers=max_parallel) a refusal in one story is persisted to .forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml and rendered in every routing exclusion with another concurrently-running story's slug.

The quarantine checks and learn calls inside _maybe_run_api_fallback, and the _learn_from_refusal call on the API-transport branch of run_agent, do not pass the caller's quiet flag, so routing exclusion and quarantine lines are logged even when the dispatch was invoked quiet.

After a process re-exec, sprint resume dispatches through run_from_dev or run_from_review without activating the persisted sprint quarantine, so a model quarantined earlier in the same sprint can reach the provider again.
A native API preference list invokes a quarantined fallback model and loses a configuration refusal from the primary whenever a later fallback succeeds.

Structured entitlement refusals from single-shot API adapters and HTTP 400 tool-loop calls reach the dispatch seam without refusal evidence or escape as exceptions, so the refused model is not quarantined.

An unattributable structured refusal is classified as transient but retains its original failure code and text, causing the DEV transient classifier to reject it as non-retryable instead of spending the bounded retry allowance.

When DEV first discovers a configuration refusal, the identity is recorded as quarantined but the current story enters infrastructure-abort handling instead of re-seating onto another eligible DEV model.
Parallel sprint stories share one mutable active-story label, so whichever story starts last can be recorded as the origin of a refusal made by a different story.
A quarantined reviewer refused at the seam is classified as a crash, included in failed reviewer metadata, and persisted as an unsuccessful capability attempt.

When a story has already cached its routing decision, a later quarantine exclusion at the dispatch seam is only logged and returned as an AgentResult, leaving that story's routing decision showing the model as included.
The escalation-advisor and decomposition-assessment non-regression cases never execute either named caller because the parameter only labels two identical direct calls to runner_cli.run_agent.

ac_verification.criterion: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the selected model is classified as a configuration refusal, distinct from a request-level or transient failure. The classification does not depend on matching one provider's message text: a refusal the classifier cannot attribute is treated as transient and retried within the existing bounded retry budget, never quarantined and never retried unboundedly.
ac_verification.evidence: src/theforge/refusal_types.py:198-213 classifies structured refusal evidence without reading detail, and tests/test_refusal_types.py:132-214 covers denial tokens, transient defaults, request-level errors, 401s, and provider prose traps. The runtime layer is incomplete because single-shot API exceptions are converted to plain AgentResult values without refusal_evidence, so those refused dispatches are never classified.; src/theforge/refusal_types.py classify_refusal reads only http_status and normalised type/code tokens (detail never consulted); requires both a denial token and a consistent status; default transient. Tests: tests/test_refusal_types.py TestClassifyRefusal including test_provider_message_text_alone_never_classifies (denial token as prose stays transient), test_a_denial_token_on_a_capacity_status_is_transient, test_a_rejected_credential_is_not_a_quarantine (401), and tests/test_model_quarantine.py test_a_transient_refusal_quarantines_nothing showing the transient path leaves the identity eligible for the existing retry machinery.; src/theforge/refusal_types.py near lines 198-213 and tests/test_refusal_types.py cover token-based classification and prose independence, but src/theforge/runners/cli.py near lines 292-306 does not translate an unattributable transient verdict into a retryable result, and src/theforge/coordinator/dev_phase.py near lines 344-350 therefore rejects unknown refusal evidence unless its text independently matches a transient pattern.

A quarantined identity requested through the seam is refused before any provider call is made, and the refusal is a routing outcome (see below). The identity checked is the identity actually dispatched: when a runner substitutes a fallback model or transport internally, the substituted identity is checked the same way, and a fallback onto a quarantined identity is refused the same way.

The decomposition assessment, the escalation advisor and the landing conflict resolver are pinned as non-regression cases: a test shows a quarantined identity is refused for at least one of the first two and for the conflict resolver. Tests: TestRunQuarantine.test_quarantine_survives_a_re_exec_of_the_same_run, test_a_later_story_in_the_same_sprint_inherits_it, test_a_new_sprint_inherits_nothing, and TestCoordinatorSeam.test_run_task_enters_the_sprint_scope_and_routing_stops_on_it.; src/theforge/model_quarantine.py near lines 299-317 and tests/test_model_quarantine.py near lines 94-123 verify persistence and key isolation at the store level, while src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py near lines 1798-1907 omits activation from the run_from_dev and run_from_review resume path used by src/theforge/sprint/runner.py near lines 2287-2318 after re-exec.

It carries a distinct marker so that transient-failure and retry classifiers in any phase never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 1 and 3 key .forge/model_quarantine/<run_id>.yaml from state.run_id, but coordinator.engine.run_task generates that ID independently for each story. sprint.runner._run_fresh receives sprint_run_id yet does not pass it to run_task, so a refusal learned by one story is written under an identity later stories never consult. The enclosing sprint also has multiple identifiers, and the plan does not select one that remains stable across os.execv generations. This predictably defeats the central cross-story, same-run quarantine requirement.
  Suggestion: Define the quarantine scope from an enclosing logical-run identifier that is shared by all sprint stories and durable across re-exec, thread it from SprintRunContext/sprint persistence into every coordinator entry point, and separately define the standalone-run scope. Test two distinct story CoordinatorState.run_id values sharing one logical run before and after re-exec.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 says to establish context only in run_task and run_from_review. Actual dispatches also originate from run_from_dev through _run_resume_coordinator and from the independent run_review_only entry point used for batch-member reviews. In addition, runners.cli.run_agent_pool calls run_agent inside new ThreadPoolExecutor threads, which do not inherit ordinary thread-local/context-variable state automatically. Therefore an ambient context installed at the named coordinator sites cannot reliably reach every review dispatch.
  Suggestion: Place setup in every state-creating entry path, including the shared resume body and run_review_only, and explicitly propagate the quarantine handle into run_agent_pool workers—or make the seam consume an explicit concurrency-safe logical-run handle whose lifetime is owned above those threads.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 normalizes configuration refusals for Codex CLI and API adapters only. run_agent also dispatches Claude, Gemini, and gh-aw CLI profiles through runner_claude.py, runner_gemini.py, and runner_ghaw.py; their failed results have no planned structured-refusal normalization. A model-access refusal on those transports will remain an ordinary or transient failure and will not be quarantined.
  Suggestion: Enumerate every supported CLI transport that can surface a provider/model-access refusal and normalize its structured error evidence, with conservative unknown-as-transient tests. If a transport cannot expose attributable evidence, state and test that limitation explicitly while ensuring any attributable form is handled.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The new YAML store is shared by concurrently executing sprint stories, but Step 1 does not mention synchronization or atomic read-modify-write behavior. Once the logical run scope is corrected, simultaneous quarantine writes can lose records or expose partial state.
  Suggestion: Specify process-local locking plus atomic persistence, and add a concurrent record/read regression test covering multiple identities in the same logical run.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk reconciliation — all three stated risks are retired, but the run-context binding in Step 3 is narrower than the seam. Binding the quarantine run context only in engine.run_task / run_from_review leaves seam calls that happen in the same run but outside those frames unquarantined: sprint intake remediation (src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:271, before run_task) and the post-run knowledge summary (coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py:421, after run_task returns) both dispatch through run_agent. No acceptance criterion pins these, and the three pinned non-phase callers are verified inside run_task's extent, so this does not block.
  Suggestion: Make the quarantine context resolvable from run_id wherever it is already known rather than only at the two engine entry points — e.g. bind it in a helper both engine and the sprint runner call once run_id exists, and have the seam treat 'no run context' as an explicit no-op it can log, so an unbound dispatch is visible rather than silently unprotected.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 says the seam returns an AgentResult with a quarantined marker, but does not say which existing field carries it. AgentResult (agent_types.py:151) is a frozen dataclass with an existing failure_code field, and api.py:141 already branches on failure_code via _MODEL_FALLBACK_FAILURE_CODES — a new failure_code value could be misread by that fallback classifier as a reason to try the next model.
  Suggestion: Have the dev agent explicitly check the quarantine marker against _MODEL_FALLBACK_FAILURE_CODES and the transport-fallback eligibility predicate in runners/api.py so a quarantine refusal cannot itself trigger a fallback attempt, and add that as an assertion in the Step 6 fallback test.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 3 sets the quarantine context only in run_task and run_from_review, but run_agent has callers outside those entry points (e.g. sprint/runner.py:271, ideate.py, triage_proposal_flow.py, cli/provider_readiness.py). The seam gate must behave sanely — no crash, no accidental enforcement of a stale run's quarantine — when no context has been set.
  Suggestion: Make the seam check a no-op when no run quarantine context is active, and have the dev agent decide explicitly which non-engine run_agent callers are in-run (and inherit the context) versus out-of-run.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Risk 1 (providers exposing only prose refusals) is retired by design — ambiguous refusals stay transient — but this means a provider whose entitlement refusal is prose-only will still be met once per story, the original #2914 symptom. That is the spec's own chosen trade-off, not a plan defect.
  Suggestion: Have Step 2 normalize the known structured shapes for all three adapters it touches (openai HTTP 400 model-access, anthropic permission_error, google PERMISSION_DENIED) so the conservative classifier covers the providers actually in the fleet.

finding_registry.description: When an API profile has a quarantined fallback model in its preference list, the primary model can fail fallback-eligible and run_api_agent still dispatches the quarantined fallback model.

When a DEV dispatch itself discovers a configuration refusal, the model is quarantined but the same failed result is returned to DEV, so the story can end on that routing refusal instead of continuing on another available model in the run.

The regression case named for the escalation advisor and decomposition assessment directly calls runner_cli.run_agent, so those caller paths can stop dispatching through the seam without this test failing.

When a configuration refusal is first discovered by a dispatch inside the DEV phase, the identity is quarantined and the retry is refused at the seam, but the story itself ends on that routing refusal rather than continuing on the remaining eligible models, because no routing checkpoint exists after the post-plan reseat.

The active-story label used to attribute quarantine records is a single module-global slot written by every concurrent run_task, so with sprint stories running in parallel on the ThreadPoolExecutor (sprint/runner.py:7573, max_workers=max_parallel) a refusal in one story is persisted to .forge/model_quarantine/<run>.yaml and rendered in every routing exclusion with another concurrently-running story's slug.

The quarantine checks and learn calls inside _maybe_run_api_fallback, and the _learn_from_refusal call on the API-transport branch of run_agent, do not pass the caller's quiet flag, so routing exclusion and quarantine lines are logged even when the dispatch was invoked quiet.

After a process re-exec, sprint resume dispatches through run_from_dev or run_from_review without activating the persisted sprint quarantine, so a model quarantined earlier in the same sprint can reach the provider again.
A native API preference list invokes a quarantined fallback model and loses a configuration refusal from the primary whenever a later fallback succeeds.

Structured entitlement refusals from single-shot API adapters and HTTP 400 tool-loop calls reach the dispatch seam without refusal evidence or escape as exceptions, so the refused model is not quarantined.

An unattributable structured refusal is classified as transient but retains its original failure code and text, causing the DEV transient classifier to reject it as non-retryable instead of spending the bounded retry allowance.

When DEV first discovers a configuration refusal, the identity is recorded as quarantined but the current story enters infrastructure-abort handling instead of re-seating onto another eligible DEV model.
A quarantined reviewer refused at the seam is classified as a crash, included in failed reviewer metadata, and persisted as an unsuccessful capability attempt.

When a story has already cached its routing decision, a later quarantine exclusion at the dispatch seam is only logged and returned as an AgentResult, leaving that story's routing decision showing the model as included.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
